title: Simran Sharma Replaces Bhavina Patel as India Flag Bearer at Para Asian Games
excerpt: The T12 sprinter will carry the flag with Pramod Bhagat at Sunday's opening ceremony in Aichi-Nagoya after officials ruled Patel must rest before her October 19 quarter-final.
body:
• Para sprinter Simran Sharma will join Pramod Bhagat as India's flag bearer at the Asian Para Games opening ceremony in Aichi-Nagoya on Sunday, October 18.
  • She replaces table tennis player Bhavina Patel, who was stood down from the ceremony so she can rest before her quarter-final on October 19.
  • The return journey to the ceremony venue takes nearly six hours, which officials judged too demanding for Patel, a wheelchair athlete, on the eve of a knockout match.
  • Sharma, a 26-year-old T12 sprinter and world champion, is targeting two gold medals in Nagoya after rebuilding her career with a new guide runner.

India has made a late change to its flag bearers for the Asian Para Games opening ceremony in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, naming para sprinter Simran Sharma alongside para badminton player Pramod Bhagat for Sunday's ceremony. Sharma replaces para table tennis player Bhavina Patel, after the Indian contingent decided Patel should rest and recover ahead of her quarter-final on Monday, October 19, according to the Paralympic Committee of India.

Rest Put Ahead of Ceremony

Patel, the Tokyo 2020 Paralympic silver medallist, had originally been named with Bhagat as India's flag bearers. The change turns on logistics: the journey to and from the ceremony venue takes nearly six hours, a heavy demand on a wheelchair athlete the day before a crucial elimination match. Officials said the decision was taken to protect her preparation rather than compromise it for a ceremonial role.

"Bhavina has her quarterfinal match on October 19, and it is important that she gets adequate rest and recovery ahead of this crucial contest. As a wheelchair athlete, travelling to and from the venue takes nearly six hours, which would be demanding and leave her with limited time to recover."

— Satyanarayana, Head Coach, Para Athletics

Satyanarayana added that the priority is to ensure athletes get the rest they need and are fully prepared to give their best when they compete. Bhagat remains a flag bearer; he has won six medals, including two gold, across the 2014, 2018 and 2023 Asian Para Games.

An Honour That Follows a Hard Year

For Sharma, 26, the honour carries weight beyond ceremony. The T12 sprinter from Uttar Pradesh is a Paralympic medallist and a world champion in the 100m, and she won two silver medals at the previous Asian Para Games running with guide runner Abhay Singh. Last year in New Delhi, running with Umar Saifi, she won gold and silver at the World Para Athletics Championships — a partnership that then unravelled after a doping case involving Saifi, shaking the trust on which a visually impaired sprinter's performance depends.

"Sometimes, I sit and cry. If the report had come two days earlier, I wouldn't have run with him."

— Simran Sharma, para sprinter, to RevSportz

Sharma now runs with a new guide, Shivam, whom she and her husband and coach Gajendra spotted in running videos online; he lives near their home in Ghaziabad. She told RevSportz the combination is still developing, noting that it generally takes three to four months to build a bond with a guide runner. A mother of two, she has spent long stretches away from her children in preparation, including seven months at a time.

What Comes Next in Nagoya

Sharma will compete in Nagoya with Shivam alongside her, targeting two gold medals including the T12 100m, where she has her sights set on the Asian record. India is fielding a 168-athlete contingent — 112 men and 56 women — across 11 disciplines at the Games, which run from October 18 to 24 with 45 nations contesting 492 medal events in 18 sports. The Paralympic Committee of India expects its strongest returns in para-athletics and para-badminton, the two sports now supplying both of India's flag bearers.
